messages:
incident-bot: :warning: High GPU queue alert for us-west-2-gpu-pool — queue length > 10k and scale at max. Paging oncall.

jenny (oncall): On it. seeing queued requests jump at 2140123400. Pulling dashboards.

jenny (oncall): Quick snapshot: queued_tokens=98M, queued_requests=11,900, autoscaler: current_nodes=96, max_nodes=96, pending_pods=320.

carlos (eng-sre): I can repro in scheduler traces — many pods request fractional MIG slices (0.25/0.5) and our placement policy is spreading by zone which created lots of tiny leftovers. Then large full-gpu jobs cannot find contiguous resources.

priya (runtime): Relevant log snippet:
```
[2140123412] placement_engine: node_available_slices=[0.25,0.25,0.0,0.125,0.375]
[2140123413] placement_engine: cannot satisfy pod xyz: need 1.0 contiguous GPU -> error code CONTIGUOUS_NOT_FOUND
```
This is classic fragmentation/stranding.

emma (customer-ops): CS reports multiple customers with timeouts on embeddings endpoints. Two enterprise tickets opened (C-9001, C-9003). ETA escalation if not resolved in 30m.

oliver (eng-platform): We have 3 mitigation paths:
- run 'defrag' to consolidate small slices into full GPUs (can be done immediately but will evict/migrate ~40 low-priority pods)
- temporarily bump autoscaler cap to 140 nodes (needs approval from infra budget owners)
- mark small/batch workloads as preemptible and shift to burst-pool.

jenny (oncall): Start defrag dry-run first: `redwoodctl node defrag --region=us-west-2 --dry-run --min-evict=10` -> suggests 38 nodes to drain, expected job time ~15m. Proceeding to run live defrag now: `redwoodctl node defrag --region=us-west-2` job id df-20260315-02.

incident-bot: Action recorded: defrag job df-20260315-02 initiated by jenny.

carlos (eng-sre): While defrag is running, I'll patch scheduler to prefer binpack for fractional requests: flipping feature-flag `placement.default_policy=binpack` in canary (10% of schedulers) to reduce new fragmentation.

priya (runtime): Note — defrag will cause short reschedules for evicted pods. We'll rate-limit eviction concurrency to avoid API storms: `--parallel=4`.

jenny (oncall): Defrag progress: 10% -> 45% after 8m. queued_requests: 11.9k -> 5.4k.

emma (customer-ops): Customers acknowledging improvement. CS sent interim status saying we're working on allocation and expect recovery in ~20m.

priya (runtime): Defrag completed. Summary:
```
job=df-20260315-02
evicted_pods=41
freed_contiguous_gpus=18
packing_ratio=0.58->0.89
queued_requests=5400->900
```
We freed enough contiguous GPUs for heavy jobs. Queue down to ~900.

carlos (eng-sre): Good. Root cause notes: mixture of tiny batch pods launching concurrently plus spread-by-zone default led to suboptimal binpacking. Autoscaler reached configured cap but didn't trigger node reclamation for fragmented slices. Filed INF-2477 for autoscaler hysteresis + fragmentation-aware scaling.

oliver (eng-platform): I've opened infra ticket INF-2477 to track: recommended changes -> (1) add fragmentation signal to autoscaler, (2) change default MIG profile to prefer 1g/8g mix in this pool, (3) enforce binpack scheduling for GPU workloads. Link: https://redwood.internal/INF-2477

jenny (oncall): Customer impact summary: ~28 minutes total elevated latency/timeouts for some customers; no data lost; CS followed up. Mitigations executed: defrag job + scheduler policy patch + temporary burst-pool routing for noncritical workloads. Follow-ups: INF-2477 and schedule a postmortem doc with timeline + metrics.

nilesh (next-oncall): Taking over at 2140123700. I'll validate there are no stranded slices and confirm defrag cleanup. Please handoff any ongoing tasks.

incident-bot: Incident auto-closed to oncall after mitigation. Postmortem requested: ping @jenny, @carlos, @priya for timeline + RCA writeup. :white_check_mark:
